page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with a constrained core count to accommodate memory-heavy architectures. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 hardware threads on an x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning is notably high, providing 64 GB of system RAM, which results in 32 GB of memory per core. Compute operations benefit from integrated hardware acceleration features including AVX-512 extensions.

Storage configurations include a bundled 322 GB local SSD for temporary scratch space and high-speed local caching. The server does not contain dedicated graphics accelerators, focusing entirely on memory-centric general computing. Microsoft Hyper-V manages underlying virtualization, ensuring dedicated CPU scheduling across the assigned vCPUs.

Benchmark outcomes reflect the architectural emphasis on high memory density over aggregate compute throughput. Single-threaded evaluation indicates standard baseline execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1265 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 23.86 GB/sec. Conversely, overall compute density is constrained by the two-thread limit, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1516 and a PassMark CPU score of 2231.39. Memory bandwidth tests yield 13.86 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 11.03 GB/sec for writes.

Cost efficiency is strongly aligned with software licensing constraints, allowing operators to reduce per-core licensing expenses while maintaining a substantial 64 GB memory footprint. The configuration is optimal for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory key-value caches like Redis, and backend enterprise services that demand large working memory without requiring extensive parallel CPU capacity.

Running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz, the instance provides 2 vCPUs from a single physical core, paired with 64 GB of RAM and 322 GB of bundled local SSD storage. It does not include a GPU. The hardware yields a substantial 32 GB of memory per vCPU, making it tailored for memory-bound applications. Benchmark testing demonstrates standard single-thread performance, reaching 1265 in Geekbench single-core tests and 23.86 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core compute is inherently restricted by the 2-vCPU architecture. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for environments constrained by per-core software licensing, making it appropriate for relational database hosting, memory-resident data stores, and light ETL processes requiring high RAM.
